w: Cast in iron and concrete on a hill so rich in quartz it gave the village of Los Andes its name, Cristo Rey rises 26 metres above Cali - 5 of them pedestal - and weighs 464 tons. It was raised on 25 October 1953, marking fifty years since the end of the War of a Thousand Days.
s: A 26-metre iron Christ on a quartz hill
_facts: 26m tall statue (5m of it pedestal) on the Cerro de los Cristales, Los Andes village west of Cali
Made of iron and concrete, weighing 464 tons
Inaugurated 25 October 1953, marking fifty years since the end of the War of a Thousand Days
Hill named for the quartz once collected in the surrounding area

w: Inside the Bank of the Republic's building in Cali's historic centre, one room holds 615 pre-Hispanic objects in gold, ceramic, stone, wood and shell, made by the Llama, Yotoco and Sonso societies. It was the bank's ninth museum and one of six across Colombia devoted to gold, and admission is free Tuesday to Saturday.
s: 615 pre-Hispanic gold pieces, one free room
_facts: Archaeological museum dedicated to the Calima culture, inside the Bank of the Republic building in Cali's historic centre
Holds 615 pre-Hispanic objects in gold, ceramic, stone, wood and shell from the Llama, Yotoco and Sonso societies
Ninth museum built by the Bank of the Republic; one of six gold museums it runs across Colombia
Free admission, open Tuesday to Saturday, with guided tours on request

w: Founded as the Museum of Modern Art La Tertulia, the complex is spread across three buildings: a gallery of 300 Colombian and international works with a children's art workshop, a print and restoration studio, and the Cinemateca, an arthouse cinema that hosts touring festivals such as EuroCine.
s: Cali's modern art museum, with its own cinema
_facts: Formerly the Museum of Modern Art La Tertulia; holds an important collection of American and especially Colombian art
Main gallery holds 300 works by national and international artists, plus a children's art workshop
Includes the Cinemateca, an arthouse cinema hosting touring film festivals such as EuroCine
A separate building houses printing and restoration workshops
